user.title: Add a server
user.description: Add one server (repeat for more). Sessions on it will run as the user you enter here.

data.name: Name
data.ha_address: Home Assistant address as seen by the server

data_description.ha_address: The server only accepts Home Assistant's key from this address. Detected automatically; change it if Home Assistant reaches the server through another address.

authorize.title: Authorize Home Assistant on {name}
authorize.description:
Home Assistant made its own SSH key for **{name}**. The key can **only** run the Agent Sessions agent: no shell, no port forwarding, and it only works from **{ha_address}**.

1. Open a terminal on **{host}** as **{user}**.
2. Paste this and press Enter:

```
{command}
```

It installs the agent to `~/.local/bin/agent-sessions` and adds the key to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Nothing else. [View the script]({script_url}) before running it.

3. It needs `python3`, `screen`, and `claude` and/or `codex` on that server. The installer checks and tells you what is missing.
4. Press **Submit**. Home Assistant connects and shows the server's fingerprint.

confirm.title: Confirm server identity
confirm.description:
Connected. Found: **{tools}** ({screen}).

Host key fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

It should match the ED25519 line the installer printed at the end. You can also check it on the server with `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`. Home Assistant will refuse to connect if it ever changes.

error.not_authorized: The server refused Home Assistant's key. Run the command above on the server as that user, then press Submit again.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the server. Check the host and port.
error.no_tools: Connected, but neither claude nor codex was found for that user. Install one and press Submit again.

abort.already_configured: This server and user are already added.
